## 2B.9 Research Note: Kishida in 2024

Bottom line: **direct accountability evidence is thin to absent**. Kishida’s 2024 public record mostly shows him insisting on lawful, civilian-protective frameworks in Ukraine and Gaza, but not publicly owning military failures or illegal conduct because Japan was not conducting the kind of operations this lens targets. The strongest negative evidence is indirect criticism that Japan kept relying on the U.S. nuclear umbrella while expanding military cooperation.

### Supports
- **[Summit on Peace in Ukraine (Summary)](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202406/15ukraine.html)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 15, 2024 | Kishida said peace in Ukraine must be “just and lasting,” grounded in the UN Charter and international law, and must not justify unilateral changes by force or coercion. He also said Japan would contribute to nuclear safety, electricity, and mine action. This is accountability-adjacent in the sense that it rejects unlawful war aims and supports civilian protection, but it is not an admission of Japan’s own wrongdoing. | `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.7`, `2B.1`

- **[Signing of the Accord on Support for Ukraine and Cooperation between the Government of Japan and Ukraine (Summary)](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202406/13accord.html)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 13, 2024 | The accord explicitly included humanitarian support, recovery/reconstruction, and cooperation under Japan’s constitutional and legal requirements. That is a legality-conscious posture, but again not an explicit acceptance of accountability for military failure or civilian harm. | `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.7`, `1B.7`

- **[G7 Leaders’ statement on Gaza](https://www.mofa.go.jp/ecm/ec/pageite_000001_00384.html)** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | June 4, 2024 | Japan joined a statement calling for hostage release, humanitarian aid, protection of civilians, compliance with international humanitarian law, and de-escalation. This is the clearest public evidence of prioritizing legal restraint and civilian protection, though it does not amount to self-accountability for Japanese military conduct. | `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.7`

- **[On the Current Situation Surrounding the Gaza Strip](https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_00630.html)** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | October 7, 2024 | Japan condemned the Hamas attacks, demanded hostage release, described Gaza’s humanitarian situation as critical, and urged all parties including Israel to comply with international humanitarian law and work toward ceasefire. This supports a finding of concern for civilian harm and legality, not a record of admitting prior Japanese wrongdoing. | `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.7`

- **[G7 Leaders’ Video Conference](https://www.mofa.go.jp/ecm/ec/pageit_000001_00279.html)** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | April 15, 2024 | Kishida said Iran’s attack on Israel would further deteriorate the situation and stressed self-restraint to prevent escalation. He also said Japan would work to protect and evacuate citizens. This is a concrete de-escalation response and a civilian-protection signal. | `2B.9`, `2B.4`, `2B.7`, `1B.8`

### Mixed / Negative
- **[Nobel prize for A-bomb survivors' group boosts hope for Japanese seeking a nuke-free world](https://apnews.com/article/808038ef664be2f200306d5e60b76711)** | Associated Press | October 11, 2024 | AP reported criticism that Kishida’s government did not sign the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons and continued relying on the U.S. nuclear umbrella while expanding military cooperation. This is indirect evidence that critics saw a gap between his disarmament rhetoric and policy, but it still does not show explicit accountability for military failures or illegal conduct. | `2B.9`, `1B.4`, `1B.6`

### Gap
- I found **no 2024 evidence** that Kishida publicly accepted responsibility for military failures, civilian casualties, illegal conduct, or false conflict justifications.
- That gap is partly structural: Japan was not running a conventional war in 2024, so the relevant accountability pattern is mostly absent from the record.
- Best calibrated conclusion: **limited direct accountability evidence; the public record is mostly restraint-oriented and legality-focused, with only indirect criticism about deterrence normalization.**
